headline: A 2017 law lets the National Science Foundation encourage its entrepreneurship programs to recruit and support women in starting businesses based on science and technology.
what_it_does: The law amends the Science and Engineering Equal Opportunities Act. It gives the National Science Foundation authority to encourage its entrepreneurial programs to recruit and support women. The goal is to help women take their research and skills beyond the lab and into the commercial world. The summary does not describe specific funding amounts or new required programs.

who_it_affects.group: Women scientists and engineers who want to start companies
who_it_affects.how: The National Science Foundation may direct its entrepreneurship programs toward recruiting and supporting them.
They are authorized to focus outreach and support on women who want to move from research into business.

when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on February 28, 2017, and the summary does not give a separate effective date.
